title: Sell Mineral Rights in Freeport, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Freeport, OH
metaDescription: Freeport sits in Harrison County, at the heart of Ohio's Utica/Point Pleasant core. See what heavy drilling activity means for your mineral value.
heroLead: Freeport sits in one of the most drilled corners of Ohio, and that density gives mineral owners here more real data to work with than almost anywhere else in the state.
intro: Freeport is a village straddling the Harrison and Guernsey county line, right in the structural core of the Utica/Point Pleasant play, where operators have drilled extensively since the early 2010s. This part of eastern Ohio was farmed and mined for coal for generations before shale arrived, and much of the mineral ownership around Freeport is fractionated across multiple heirs from those older family farms.

sections.heading: Heavy development and what it means for valuation
paragraphs: Freeport's position in the core fairway has meant significant horizontal drilling activity over the past decade, which typically translates into real production history for tracts in the area. A producing interest here usually comes with royalty statements showing your exact decimal share, which is far more reliable for pricing than a general estimate based on county averages.

sections.heading: Fractionated ownership from generations of farm inheritance
paragraphs: Because so much of the land around Freeport was originally farmed and passed down through multiple generations, it's common for a single original tract's minerals to now be split among a dozen or more heirs, each holding a small fraction. Confirming your exact share requires a title search through either the Harrison or Guernsey County Recorder, depending on which side of the line your parcel falls.

faqs.question: Which county recorder handles Freeport-area title searches?
faqs.answer: It depends on which side of the county line your specific parcel sits on, since Freeport straddles Harrison and Guernsey counties. Your deed's legal description will show which county it's recorded in.

faqs.question: Why do so many owners here only hold a small fraction of a mineral interest?
faqs.answer: Because minerals under an original farm tract typically pass to all the owner's heirs in equal shares, and after two or three generations without consolidation, a once-whole interest can be split among many descendants.

faqs.question: How current does a royalty statement need to be to price my interest?
faqs.answer: Recent statements, ideally from the past year, give the clearest picture of current production and value, since older statements may not reflect how a well has moved along its decline curve.

faqs.question: How do I know if my Freeport interest has ever been abandoned under the Dormant Mineral Act?
faqs.answer: Check the recorder's index in the applicable county for any affidavit of abandonment filed against your name or a prior owner's name, and respond within the 60-day window if one has been served.
